insight.headline: The offense hasn't matched the pitching.
insight.detail: The staff is holding at 3.96 ERA, but a .654 OPS at the plate has made it difficult. San Francisco sits at 6-4 over their last ten with neither side pulling ahead.
insight.why: ERA at 3.96 · quiet bats (.654 OPS) · 6–4 in the last ten

narrative.top_frame: A shutout feels like a reset until you realize they couldn't score at all.
narrative.what_this_means: The Giants and Phillies played scoreless baseball on a night when the Phillies couldn't hit anything. That should have been the story. Instead, it became proof that this team's offense is not just streaky anymore. It is fragile. Down 6.0 games in the division, they cannot afford nights where nobody finds a gap, nobody works into traffic, nobody delivers one swing that opens a door. The pattern used to be inconsistency. Now it looks like a team running on fumes. A 0-0 game decided by nothing means nothing was there to begin with. This isn't a slump anymore. This is how stretches collapse.
narrative.what_to_watch: Now the question is whether Webb can force the Phillies to produce against a team that just watched both offenses go silent. A weak .223 average is only favorable if the Giants' bats show up to punish it.
